prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Solar PV capacity additions by country and quarter, 2024 (MW) (language en).
Grid: 9 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Segment" spans 1 col × 3 row; "Europe" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Asia-Pacific" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Germany" spans 2 col × 1 row; "France" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Japan" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Australia" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Segment" · longest unbreakable word 86px · one-line width 172px
  col 2: header "Europe › Germany › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 3: header "Europe › Germany › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "Europe › France › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 33px · one-line width 33px
  col 5: header "Europe › France › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 6: header "Asia-Pacific › Japan › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 7: header "Asia-Pacific › Japan › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 8: header "Asia-Pacific › Australia › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 9: header "Asia-Pacific › Australia › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1A: widths [107, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61] · table 596×384px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 236px
Design r1B: widths [107, 61, 61, 59, 59, 59, 59, 59, 59] · table 584×384px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 224px
Design r1C: widths [107, 61, 61, 54, 59, 59, 59, 59, 59] · table 579×384px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 219px
Design r2A: widths [107, 63, 63, 63, 63, 63, 63, 63, 63] · table 612×384px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 252px
Design r2B: widths [107, 62, 62, 62, 62, 62, 62, 62, 62] · table 604×384px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 244px
Design r2C: widths [107, 63, 63, 63, 63, 61, 61, 61, 61] · table 604×384px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 244px
Design r3A: widths [107, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61] · table 596×384px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 236px
Design r3B: widths [195, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61, 61] · table 684×291px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 324px

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
